claim: A model's internal calibration/accuracy signal and its verbalized confidence score are both linearly encoded in activation space but occupy orthogonal directions, consistent across three open-weight models and four datasets.
stance_target: internal-knowledge and verbalized self-report are geometrically/mechanistically dissociated in the model's representations
scope_conditions: General QA/reasoning datasets (domain not specified as code in abstract); three open-weight LLMs, four datasets; whole-answer verbalized confidence
quoted_support: we present a mechanistic interpretability analysis of verbalized confidence, using linear probes and contrastive activation addition (CAA) steering to show that calibration and verbalized confidence signals are encoded linearly but are orthogonal to one another -- a finding consistent across three open-weight models and four datasets.

claim: When models are prompted to simultaneously reason through a problem and verbalize a confidence score, the reasoning process disrupts the verbalized-confidence direction in activation space, worsening miscalibration -- termed the 'Reasoning Contamination Effect.'
stance_target: verbalized confidence is causally corrupted by concurrent reasoning, widening the gap from the true internal accuracy signal
scope_conditions: General QA/reasoning; joint reason-then-verbalize-confidence prompting setup
quoted_support: Interestingly, when models are prompted to simultaneously reason through a problem and verbalize a confidence score, the reasoning process disrupts the verbalized confidence direction, exacerbating miscalibration. We term this the 'Reasoning Contamination Effect.'

claim: A two-stage adaptive steering pipeline that reads the model's internal accuracy estimate and steers verbalized output toward it substantially improves calibration alignment across all evaluated models.
stance_target: internal knowledge can be used to correct/close the verbalization faithfulness gap via activation steering
scope_conditions: General QA/reasoning, whole-answer verbalized confidence, activation steering intervention
quoted_support: Leveraging this insight, we introduce a two-stage adaptive steering pipeline that reads the model's internal accuracy estimate and steers verbalized output to match it, substantially improving calibration alignment across all evaluated models.

claim: This paper establishes the internal-knowledge-vs-verbalized-confidence faithfulness gap mechanistically (orthogonal encoding directions) at whole-answer granularity in general QA/reasoning domains, not on code generation and not decomposed per-requirement/per-unit-test -- the closest precedent found to the proposed pivot's core framing, raising real adjacent-novelty risk if the pivot is not clearly differentiated by domain (code) and granularity (per-requirement).
stance_target: does this paper scoop the internal-knowledge-vs-self-report faithfulness gap framing at per-requirement code granularity?
scope_conditions: Comparison of this paper's scope against the proposed AAAI-27 pivot
quoted_support: Large language models (LLMs) tend to verbalize confidence scores that are largely detached from their actual accuracy, yet the geometric relationship governing this behavior remain poorly understood.
